sentences.text: 2. Counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the aforementioned crime.
He is suffering jail NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9702 2 CRA-2473-2025 incarceration since 15.01.2025.

He further submits that the complainant/victim was carrying the business of selling the saree and she went to Khargone and in between she came in contact with the appellant and has developed relations with him.
It is stated that on 15.10.2024, the appellant has committed rape with the complainant but the FIR has been lodged on 26.12.2024 with a delay of about two years.
He also submits that due to said relationship between appellant and complainant/victim a baby girl was born out.

It is a clear case of consensual relationship, therefore no offence has been committed by the appellant and the fact that victim is a married lady and has not taken divorce from her husband and the appellant is also a married person.
He submits that conclusion of trial will take considerably long time to conclude.
On these grounds, counsel for the appellant prays for grant of bail to appellant.
3. Per contra, public prosecutor for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text: 4. Counsel for the complainant/victim has also opposed the prayer on the ground that complainant was cheated by the appellant on the false pretext of marriage thereby committed rape upon her.

A notice was given to the appellant on 08.12.2024 for adopting the complainant and her daughter but he did not reply to the allegations contained in the notice and therefore FIR was lodged against the appellant and hence he is not entitled for any leniency and prays for dismissal of criminal appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9702 3 CRA-2473-2025 5.
Heard the rival contentions of both the counsels and perused the record.

6. In the aforesaid factual backdrop, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that victim is a married lady and without taking divorce from her legal husband has developed intimacy with the appellant and has later developed physical relationship by giving a birth to a girl child.
Later the relations turn sour and thereafter FIR was lodged against the present appellant.
Hence, this Court is inclined to grant bail to appellant.
Accordingly, without commenting on merits of the case, the appeal is allowed.

7. It is directed that appellant - Raju @ Rudra S/o Ramesh Rathore be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the tune of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand) with separate solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court, for his regular appearance before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by the said Court, without any default, during trial.
The appellant shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023.
8. The appellant will not indulge himself in any criminal activity in future.

This order shall be effective till the end of trial, however, in case of bail jump and or any breach of any of the conditions of bail, the prosecution will be at liberty to move appropriate application for cancellation of bail.

9. The concerned Court shall get the conditions reproduced on the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:9702 4 CRA-2473-2025 personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.
If any of them is unable to write, the scribe shall certify that he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused on the surety.
10. Accordingly, the criminal appeal stands allowed and is disposed of, in above terms.
11. Certified copy, as per Rules.
